reason: Reproduced read-only. The SI rule in force (CONTEXT l.3404 RESUME POINT (d); R21-A9 (v); R22-A4(B)) says SI = the BASE's DIVINS settings. runbook.notes.md section 9 (l.206-209) still has DIVINS_CAP=4 with REF=exp58_x138_safe_lowref. Gating the cap-6 exp70g notebook against exp58 FAILs notebook-bytes ('8 hunk(s) vs 8 (1 extra, 1 missing)'). Against exp70g it PASSes (8 hunks, +976/-4, identical; INFO 'not a pinned final recipe'). Against exp78a it also PASSes. So the runbook either ships K2's cap 4 or drops the port to (C). The fix is a documentation edit that aligns the runbook with an already-registered rule. It adds no new mechanism, no knob ladder and no submit, and the builder needs no --lab (SUCC_KNOBS has no cap limit). The finding's 'same order' point is load-bearing: build_probe_kernel.py l.2961 writes the os.environ lines in --set order. exp78a sets CAP/FRAME_CAP after LOWREFINE_ENABLE, so the runbook's split '$K $TL --set LOWREFINE_ENABLE=1' matches only the exp70g order. The finding misses two related gaps. (1) The runbook l.212 fallback (DET_THRESHOLD != 0.965: K1 recipe, LOWREFINE_ENABLE=0, REF=exp58t_x138_safe) has the same defect. exp58t is the only non-lab lowrefine-off insertion build on disk, and it is cap 4, so a BASE-cap K1 SI would FAIL too. (2) The fork expectation '+5..+25 (x138->K2 +13)' is BASE-dependent. Dummy forks are x138 62, K2 75, exp70g 81 (+19), exp78a 86 (+24) and exp78b 95 (+33), so with BASE = exp78b a correct SI would look out of range. Value caveat: this only matters if E10 fires (a public notebook at >= 0.957) before the deadline, which is unlikely. The cap-6-over-cap-4 edge is one public embryo and says nothing about private.
fix: Edit research/wf_ideas_v4/e10v3/runbook.notes.md section 9 and the E10 v3 NOW line (text only; do not restart the loop). (a) Build the SI with the --set flags taken from the BASE folder's probe.json 'change' in exactly that order, without DEGRADE_KEEP_DIV/PATCHES (safetail sets those). Set REF=experiments/<BASE> (now exp70g_k2_cap6, nb 52c182a3; exp78a 8d8d9c28 or exp78b d54d810c if W1 moves BASE). Treat INFO 'reference build = not a pinned final recipe' as expected, and change the runbook's 'expect ... K2 final exp58 recipe' line to match. One-liner: K=$(python -c "import json;c=json.load(open('experiments/<BASE>/probe.json'))['change'];print(' '.join(f'--set {k}={v}' for k,v in c.items() if k not in ('DEGRADE_KEEP_DIV','PATCHES')))"). Then call build_probe_kernel.py ... --patch divinsert --patch safetail --patch lowrefine $K, with no separate $TL or LOWREFINE flag. (b) Fallback for DET_THRESHOLD != 0.965: first build a local x138 reference with the same K but LOWREFINE_ENABLE=0 (python tools/build_probe_kernel.py exp73ref_k1_<base> --base x138 --patch divinsert --patch safetail --patch lowrefine <K with LOWREFINE_ENABLE=0>; 1 s, never pushed). Use it as REF, since exp58t is cap 4 only. Pre-build it now so the SI gate is rehearsed. (c) Replace the forks line with 'forks added ~ BASE dummy delta vs x138 (62): exp70g +19, exp78a +24, exp78b +33; flag if outside 0.5x-2x of that delta'. Optionally, at the gate's next planned edit, add the BASE nb sha to SI_REF_KNOWN.
realistic_gain: Operational rather than score: it avoids a wasted 25-35 min SI dummy and a fall to (C), or shipping cap 4 instead of the BASE, in the unlikely case that E10 fires before the deadline. Expected LB effect ~0 unless E10 fires. If it fires, the SI then carries the best-scored insertion config (public +0.002 for cap 6 over cap 4 on one embryo; private transfer unproven). Cost: ~10 min of text edits plus one 1-s local reference build.
